title: Decomposition topology ruling (SO cycle): converge on crosslink swarm-from-one-doc vs keep hand-split slice docs

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: FINDING (verified against crosslink source @ 6b4f736f, binary==source; full report on #826 session 2026-08-01): crosslink's intended decomposition is ONE governing design doc that 'crosslink swarm init --doc' splits into phase-gated, dependency-ordered agent waves, guided by '### Layer N:'/'### Phase N:' H3 headers under '## Requirements' (swarm.qmd:17, init.rs:143-249). kickoff is single-feature only; kickoff plan does NOT decompose (plan.rs:44-48). There is NO parent->child linkage between .design docs (PipelineState/DesignDoc carry no such field). Our pattern — parent contract + hand-split slice docs (composition-slice, install-slice, gate-execution-slice, routing-before-fix-guardrail, finding-query-join), each independently kicked off — is a hand-rolled workaround: legal per-doc, invisible as a program, forgoing swarm's phase gates/ordering/budget windows. The contract itself names the manual-dispatch fallback as 'must not calcify' — it calcified. DECISION FOR SO CYCLE: (a) converge on swarm-from-one-doc (restructure contract Requirements with Layer/Phase H3 headers; retire slice pipelines), or (b) ratify the slice-doc pattern as vsdd's deliberate topology with tracker-level parent linkage. DEPENDENCIES: #837 (kickoff plan agents stall — same infra swarm rides), #846 + #847 (upstream bugs found in this audit), swarm live fire never run. Operator directive 2026-08-01: own issue + SO cycle, not rushed into cleanup PR #19.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: OPERATOR INITIAL READ (2026-08-01, re-scopes this issue): Q8's finding is a DEVIATION TO REMEDIATE, not a candidate pattern to possibly ratify. Two deliverables for the SO cycle: (1) REMEDIATION — fix what we've already done: restructure the contract's Requirements with the '### Layer N:'/'### Phase N:' H3 headers crosslink's parser consumes (design_doc.rs:159-165), re-parent/retire the hand-split slice-doc pipelines, re-enter the intended one-doc->swarm flow. Upstream dependency stays visible: #837 (kickoff agents stall) may block the LIVE swarm fire, not the restructuring. (2) PREVENTION — revise the methodology harness so this class of deviation cannot silently persist: the contract's 'fallback must not calcify' clause was prose with NO fire-check (authored-not-exercised, the #840 governing law hitting the methodology itself — it calcified undetected). Control shape: a DEVIATION REGISTRY — every off-affordance act / persisted bootstrap fallback carries a recorded entry with stated reason + retest trigger + expiry; a check enumerates standing deviations and fails loud on fired-trigger-or-lapsed-expiry without re-evaluation. Extends the act-to-affordance map + hand-rolled-affordance fixture; exercise-registry pattern applied to standing workarounds. Grade path: convention -> CI-backed block. NOT riding cleanup PR #19 (new control design, not a migration); this cycle is its home, with the topology remediation as founding evidence.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: CORRECTIVE NOTE (SO-F1, design cold-review round 1): earlier comments on this issue (2026-08-01 19:37 and 19:41) assert the contract 'names the manual-dispatch fallback as must not calcify' — that phrase does NOT appear in .design/agent-first-vsdd-toolkit.md (repo-wide grep confirms). It was this orchestrator's paraphrase from the #840 grounding-audit context, propagated as if quoted contract text. The contract's ACTUAL clauses: line ~131 (Conformance at action time) — hand-rolling an equivalent while the affordance exists 'carries a stated reason or is nonconformant', with the evidence line that no crosslink workflow was ever self-summoned; plus the bootstrap 'until' clauses. The prevention deliverable's premise stands on those real clauses (stronger, if anything: a stated-reason rule with no fire-check is exactly the gap the deviation registry closes). The design doc's Summary will be re-grounded accordingly in the fix pass; future citations of this issue should quote line 131, not the paraphrase.
